title: The High Lichen Frontier

features.name: lichen colony ascending
features.desc-on-touch: You trace the slow archive written in colour across the stone face. Each mark is a decade. The lichen is reading weather the same way Katita read corruption: line by line, asking what changed.

features.name: frontier scatter-field
features.desc-on-touch: The growth here has learned not to cluster. Each organism trusts the space between itself and the next—a grammar of distance that lets this high country breathe.

features.name: stone study plaque
features.desc-on-touch: Field notes laminated and sealed: lichen study from 1987, Katita's hand identifying growth rates, margins, colour-shift per altitude. The archive's own measuring hand, made visible.

features.name: sky-roof optical pool
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of high-altitude light that seems to gather the blue of the sky itself. When you look down, you see the lichen's view upward—colour mapped in reverse.

features.name: altitude wire-tower
features.desc-on-touch: A tall wireframe structure that models the frontier itself—how growth scatters as oxygen thins, how distance becomes the defining architecture of all living things here.

inscription: here the slow colours learned that growth need not gather to be profound

file.name: HighCountry_Lichen_Transect_1987_Katita.txt
file.note: Growth rate studies at altitude: every 100m the colour-shift accelerates, as if lichen remembers earlier light.

reverie.title: REVERIE — high country at noon, lichen under fingertip
narr: You kneel on the stone where she kneels, reading the slow
record written in lichen. Her hand traces the margin where
growth stops—where altitude teaches every living thing its
honest limit. She looks up. The sky here is so direct it hurts.
The lichen did not fail. The lichen knew exactly how high to grow.

exits.label: downward where lichen fades and trees remember their roots
toward a high pass where weather forgets which way to move
further up where even stone becomes sparse
across a ridge where lichen meets the view of distant valleys
